content:
Ava (PM): Heads-up — milestone Alpha-3 slipped ~3w because the runtime memory regression popped during integration. We need a quick cut list for MVP vs v1 by EOD Friday so we can lock the launch date. I sketched 3 candidate cuts below, please reply with impact/risks and a one-line recommendation.

Candidates (my initial take):
1) Defer multi-model routing (only single-model routes in MVP). saves ~2w of infra work but blocks some partner use-cases.
2) Ship backend caching + APIs but hide Cache Dashboard (defer full UX). saves ~1.5w design/front-end work.
3) Remove dynamic canary traffic shaping (static canaries only, no runtime policies). reduces rollout complexity but weakens staged rollouts.

Luca (Eng): Multi-model is the biggest lift. We can ship single-model routes and add a `routing_version` flag to the API to make v1->v2 rollout smoother. Recommend cut 1 for MVP.

Maya (Design): Cache Dashboard is ~3 full sprints to polish (filters, retention controls). We can ship minimal indicators (hit rate, miss rate) in Console Metrics and hide the full dashboard behind a feature flag. Cut 2 seems reasonable.

Priya (Solutions): Customers doing heavy LLM pipelines (Acme, Nova) will complain about no multi-model routing. But they are ok with no fancy dashboard as long as backend metrics are accessible via API. If we keep backend telemetry + simple Console metrics, we preserve most customer value.

Diego (Sales): Major enterprise pilot (Acme) prioritized SSO, dedicated capacity, and SLAs over the Cache UI. Their ask for multi-model is real but they said they can accept a phased approach if we commit to v1 timeline. Sales prefers cuts 2+3, keep multi-model as a clear v1 deliverable.

Sam (SRE): Dynamic canary policies introduce sources of state and DB churn. For safety, static canaries only for MVP is lower risk. Also agree to preserve backend caching (so infra load is reduced). Cut 3 recommended.

Nisha (CTO): Prioritize reliability and deterministic rollouts. My preference: keep backend caching, do single-model routes with API flag, and defer dashboard + dynamic shaping. That maps to cuts 2+3. Makes the launch predictable and still gives customers routing hooks for v1.

Ava (PM): Synthesizing: Proposed MVP scope = core API (single-model routes + `routing_version` flag), backend caching enabled, minimal Console metrics, static canaries only. v1 includes multi-model routing, Cache Dashboard, and dynamic shaping.

Quick asks: owners please confirm these two things by EOD Friday:
- Luca: "I can scope the `routing_version` flag + single-model runtime changes to a 2-week ship if we deprioritize dynamic shaping?"
- Maya/Priya: "Can we ship minimal Console metrics (hit/miss, avg latency) by mid-MVP and hide deeper dashboard behind feature flag?"

Luca (Eng): Yes on the flag — 2w looks doable if we freeze shaping. Will open a 3-part PR: runtime, API flag, tests.

Maya (Design): Yes we can deliver minimal metrics panel. Will drop detailed wireframes into the Figma file and mark the dashboard as 'v1'.

Priya (Solutions): We'll update the pilot docs and tell Acme/Nova the phased plan. Will collect any hard blocker signals by tomorrow AM.

release-bot: Deploy window updated: Alpha-3 -> postponed 3 weeks. New tentative launch: 2026-05-17.

Ava (PM): OK — thanks everyone. If no objections by EOD Friday I will lock MVP cuts (2+3) and update roadmap + PRD. :thumbsup:

Diego (Sales): :thumbsup: will communicate to Acme that multi-model is scheduled for v1 but we have routing flags for future proofing.

Sam (SRE): Noted. I'll run the static canary playbook and add the rollback checklist to the release doc.

Nisha (CTO): Good tradeoff. Keep focus on observability and SLOs for this ship.

Ava (PM): Closing thread — thank you. If anyone has late objections DM me.
